note: Each eval needs a repository whose history holds a pull request with the named mechanism; run it from that checkout. The runner writes the PR's changed-file list as a JSON list to pr_files.json in each run directory, and may write ground_truth.json mapping an assertion ID to the strings the page must quote (for example the old and new patterns for both_patterns_verbatim). check_mechanical.py reports an assertion as not applicable when its file is absent.

evals.name: ca-bundle-incident
evals.prompt: teach me the PR in this repo that added a custom CA bundle to our TLS settings — I need to understand the CA bundle thing well enough to explain it to the team on Monday
evals.expected_output: Self-contained HTML artifact teaching the pull request. Should identify the spine (the custom TLS `ca` option replaces Node's default trust store rather than extending it, so supplying a few private certs silently drops every bundled public root), map every changed file the PR touches, and include an operable element — most naturally a trust-store composition toggle.
assertions: standalone_html: one complete HTML document with no external script or style URLs
file_map_complete: every file the PR changes is named in the page
selfcheck_present: 6 to 14 predict-then-check questions in any form
interaction_simulates_model: an operable element runs this PR's own mechanism, not a quiz
page_weight_reasonable: embedded fonts stay under 120 KB and weigh less than the page content
real_error_string: quotes the real UNABLE_TO_GET_ISSUER_CERT_LOCALLY error
spine_identified: explains that the custom ca option replaces Node's default trust store rather than extending it, dropping the bundled public roots

evals.name: redos-regex
evals.prompt: can you help me understand the PR in this repo that fixed the slow validation regex — I'm reviewing some similar regex code and I want to actually get why the old pattern was slow, not just be told it was
evals.expected_output: Self-contained HTML artifact teaching the pull request. Should identify the spine (an outer quantifier wraps a group whose own quantifier can already consume the same characters, so the matcher has exponentially many ways to split the same string), include a live regex input or complexity demo that actually runs both patterns, and surface any reviewer concern left unresolved at merge, quoted rather than paraphrased.
assertions: standalone_html: one complete HTML document with no external script or style URLs
file_map_complete: every file the PR changes is named in the page
selfcheck_present: 6 to 14 predict-then-check questions in any form
interaction_simulates_model: an operable element runs this PR's own mechanism, not a quiz
page_weight_reasonable: embedded fonts stay under 120 KB and weigh less than the page content
both_patterns_verbatim: shows the old and new patterns exactly as the PR has them
spine_identified: explains that the outer quantifier wraps a group whose inner quantifier can already match the same characters, so one string splits exponentially many ways
reviewer_concern_surfaced: reports any unresolved reviewer concern from the review thread, or states that none was raised

evals.name: asyncio-lock-race
evals.prompt: walk me through the PR in this repo that fixed the cached asyncio lock, I have to answer questions about it
evals.expected_output: Self-contained HTML artifact teaching the pull request. Should identify the spine (asyncio.Lock only binds to a loop on its contended acquire path, so an orphaned waiter poisons the cached lock for every later caller on another event loop), include a steppable timeline or interleaving explorer, and report the PR's merge state and any outstanding review honestly.
assertions: standalone_html: one complete HTML document with no external script or style URLs
file_map_complete: every file the PR changes is named in the page
selfcheck_present: 6 to 14 predict-then-check questions in any form
interaction_simulates_model: an operable element runs this PR's own mechanism, not a quiz
page_weight_reasonable: embedded fonts stay under 120 KB and weigh less than the page content
poisoning_explained: names the lock's _waiters queue and its bound _loop when explaining how one orphaned waiter poisons the cached lock
spine_identified: explains that asyncio.Lock binds to a loop only on its contended acquire path
merge_state_honest: reports the merge state honestly, including whether the PR merged with a review still requesting changes
